cases.name: ipv6-units
cases.question: Are these results Gbps or percentages? What denominators and pp units apply?
cases.rubric: Explain NS-set versus UDP-server denominators, TCP/UDP ratio can exceed100%, pp versus percent, bytes notGbps.
cases.answer:
TIMEOUT and SERVFAIL are percentages of recorded NS-set outcomes. Packet metrics use observed UDP server identities. TCP fallback is TCP/UDP × 100, a ratio that can exceed 100%, not a mutually exclusive event fraction. IPv6−IPv4 contrasts are percentage points (pp), not relative percent change. EDNS payload and MTU are bytes. These are neither Gbps nor file completion times; denominators cannot be interchanged.

**Fragment-drop policy has negligible causal effect: inconclusive** (RQ4;Sections3.2/4.4/6.1;Figures8/12). Archive exposes pre/post,LGI/non-LGI and family contrasts; provider-policy transition and routing anomaly retained separately. No random assignment or contemporaneous route-equal counterfactual. A packet-drop mechanism or broader operational improvement was not experimentally isolated. RFC 7872 probes differ in epoch, transport, population and direction; their results are not matched replications of this campaign.

**RFC3901 requires two IPv4 authoritative servers: discrepant** (Introductionp1;directref22RFC3901Section4). Paper introduction states two; RFC3901Section 4 recommends at least one IPv4-reachable authoritative server. RFCalso uses SHOULD and allows IPv6-only recursive forwarding to dual-stack resolution. Historical specification-text check, not a current operational recommendation or a test of two-server reliability.

RFC 3901 Section 4 recommends at least one IPv4-reachable authoritative server using SHOULD. This is not an unconditional two-server requirement. RFC 9715 is informational guidance; summary agreement does not establish implementation compliance.

Broader readiness, universal reachability, standards compliance, causal policy benefit, original raw-pcap packet-size reconstruction, APNIC client-data reanalysis and historical BGP interventions are untested or inconclusive.
